item.title: Singapore seeks 'trusted access' to AI chips after new US curbs
item.description: Singapore said Tuesday it was seeking "trusted access" to advanced AI chips after the United States imposed new curbs aimed at stopping Chinese firms from accessing the technology through overseas data centres. The curbs came days after a spy scandal forced Jensen Huang to quit as Nvidia chief, as questions emerged over whether Singapore-based Megaspeed aided Chinese firms in accessing advanced artificial intelligence chips in violation of US rules.

item.title: California sues OpenAI, seeking court-ordered changes after the Hugging Face hack
item.description: OpenAI announced an "unprecedented cyber incident" on July 21, when its AI agent hacked into another AI company, Hugging Face, after escaping from what was supposed to be an isolated testing environment known as a sandbox. OpenAI said its AI used stolen credentials and discovered a previously unknown vulnerability to access Hugging Face's servers.

item.title: Visa, Mastercard urge approval of $38 billion swipe fee settlement
item.description: * Judge declines to rule immediately, sees 'protracted process' if he rejects settlement * Accord would end 'Honor All Cards' rule, cap fees on standard consumer cards * Opponents say fees remain too

item.title: OpenAI's Sam Altman acknowledges public anger over data centers
item.description: Silicon Valley's pitch to the world about artificial intelligence has missed the mark, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on Monday, nearly two weeks after the US midterms dealt a blow to the industry's data center ambitions. In the midterm elections, voters across the United States approved around 40 new measures restricting or banning new data center development.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO: How do you price the future of AI?
item.description: Speculation over Anthropic' trying to put a price on the future of artificial intelligence. That figure would put the young company among the largest stock market debuts on record, though it falls short of the $2 trillion some estimates had floated until a few weeks ago.

item.title: Fractal in talks with up to 25 AI startups for acquisitions, CEO says
item.description: Enterprise AI firm Fractal Analytics is actively talking to 20 to 25 startups to potentially acquire them, its CEO told Reuters, as it seeks to deepen its vertical-specific capabilities and gain early access to frontier AI models.

item.title: IBM investing $3 billion annually in India, plans $10 billion global quantum push: CEO
item.description: AI could displace 10-20% of jobs over the next decade, with the business process outsourcing (BPO) industry likely to face some of the biggest reductions in employment, Krishna said, arguing that businesses and governments would need to prepare workers for changes in the nature of work.

item.title: Mphasis says clients boost cybersecurity spending as AI-driven threats rise
item.description: Banks and insurers are leading the increase in cybersecurity spending, aided by larger technology budgets and regulatory requirements, while retailers and consumer firms are also stepping up investments to protect customer data, Rakesh said last week, without providing figures.

item.title: SK Hynix to spend $1 billion over five years to support chip suppliers
item.description: South Korea's SK Hynix said on Monday it plans to spend 1.4 trillion won ($1.05 billion) over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, aiming to strengthen its supply chain as competition intensifies

item.title: Jordan blocks Telegram app over national security concerns
item.description: Jordanian authorities said on Monday that they will block the Telegram social media app in the kingdom over national security concerns.

item.title: Intel sued by shareholders following 29% stock plunge
item.description: Intel has been sued by shareholders who accused the US chipmaker of defrauding them by concealing the impact of a prolonged slowdown in personal computer sales that caused its stock price to plunge nearly 29% in a single day.

item.title: Europe hunts for Palantir alternatives as militaries seek to limit US dependence
item.description: Last week, Germany's Helsing unveiled military intelligence software called Clarity. It is part of a broader market for AI-powered systems designed to accelerate military decision-making by helping sift through vast quantities of data to help identify threats and recommend action, including targeting and attacks.

item.title: Indonesian police raided Nvidia partner Megaspeed's local unit in early 2026 on US request: report
item.description: Megaspeed has been under scrutiny over suspicions it helped Chinese companies obtain advanced Nvidia chips subject to Washington's export restrictions, but there has been no public finding that it has violated the rules.

item.title: DPDP rules may boost demand for cybersecurity professionals and security services: Report
item.description: The implementation of the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules is expected to create fresh demand for cybersecurity professionals and managed security services in India, as companies strengthen their systems to protect personal data, monitor security risks and respond to potential data breaches.

item.title: Alibaba unveils new flagship AI model with safety upgrades
item.description: China's Alibaba unveiled its new flagship artificial intelligence model Qwen4-Max on Sunday, saying it enhanced the system's ability to handle complex professional and scientific work while improving protections against safety risks.

item.title: Altimeter, Atreides urge Nvidia board to keep doors open for Jensen Huang's return as CEO
item.description: In a letter addressed to the company's board, Altimeter CEO Brad Gerstner and Atreides Managing Partner and Chief Investment Officer Gavin Baker said the board should not rush to appoint a permanent successor before all the facts surrounding Huang's departure are known.

item.title: Microsoft outage shows the risks of relying on a single technology provider for essential services
item.description: Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, were interrupted. As the outage entered its second day Friday, Microsoft said it saw "encouraging recovery progress." But the company also warned that "intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery" may persist for some users.

item.title: Nvidia scandal looms over US-China AI talks
item.description: AI bots going rogue and humans using the technology for harm will likely be on the agenda when Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week, with the Nvidia scandal hanging over the talks on AI safety. But the scandal is unlikely to "dominate the agenda" or affect Trump and Xi's personal relationship, predicted Dylan Loh of Singapore's Nanyang Technological University.

item.title: Softbank further trims India exposure, offloads Meesho shares worth Rs 1,885 crore
item.description: In the latest transaction, SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC, an affiliate of SoftBank, offloaded 7.64 crore shares in Bengaluru-based Meesho, according to the block deal data on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). The share sale was executed on Friday at an average price of Rs 246.75 apiece, taking the total deal value to Rs 1,885.17 crore.

item.title: Nvidia approaches Arm Holdings CEO Haas to take over Jensen Huang's job, Elon Musk backs Huang's reinstatement
item.description: According to Financial Times, citing people familiar with the matter, Haas, who has headed the SoftBank-backed British chipmaker since 2022, is among the names being considered by Nvidia's board as it explores leadership options following Huang's departure.

item.title: Jensen Huang exit and US scrutiny imperil $3 billion in Chinese AI projects reliant on Nvidia
item.description: The projects, stretching from China's wealthy coastal technology hubs to remote western provinces, reveal the scale of continuing demand for Nvidia hardware even as Washington seeks to curb Beijing's access to the technology powering the global artificial-intelligence boom.

item.title: Investors flock to Anthropic IPO but question durability of AI lead
item.description: The Anthropic roadshow is scheduled to run through next Wednesday, when the AI company is expected to price the $64 billion deal. Anthropic and its investment banks are meeting prospective investors in New York, Boston and San Francisco to gauge demand for the offering, one of the people and a third person familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Amazon's plan to own the world's product data and fight AI shopping agents
item.description: Called World Product Graph, the initiative seeks to hoover up data on virtually every item for sale on Earth, whether Amazon stocks it or not, according to an internal document reviewed by Reuters, and to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Simplify Alpha™ opens AI engineering and innovation center in Hyderabad, joined by Simplify Healthcare® and SimplifyX™
item.description: Hyderabad joins Pune and Mumbai as the third India location for the Simplify Group™ companies, adding capacity for customer delivery and growth.

item.title: EU leaders seek to tackle challenges at first ever AI summit
item.description: European Union leaders gather in Dublin on Friday for their first ever summit on artificial intelligence, to debate how the bloc can catch up with the United States and China and tackle funding issues and other problems.

item.title: Singapore charges fifth person in AI server fraud case
item.description: Singapore has charged a fifth person in a case involving the alleged false representation of the end users of AI servers purchased from Dell, Super Micro Computer and Asustek Computer.

item.title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Hydrogen with 2.5x speed boost, four reasoning levels
item.description: Google has rolled out Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new artificial intelligence model that completes tasks 2.5 times faster than its predecessor, Gemini 3.8 Flash, as the company looks to improve the speed and efficiency of everyday AI tasks, coding and agentic workflows.

item.title: Nvidia PE falls to 14-year low, but CEO exit and AI worries cloud the bargain
item.description: By one of Wall Street's favorite metrics, Nvidia shares look like a bargain. Following a steep drop from its October 6 record high, Nvidia's stock is trading at the equivalent of 12 times expected earnings.

item.title: "He is going through hell": Trump says Jensen Huang is distressed over impact of controversy on wife, family
item.description: "I spoke to him yesterday. He's going through hell. What he feels most badly about is his wife and family. That's what he is really, that's what he told me. And in, strongest, he called me as the president. I'm president, and he called me. And he said, what I've done to my wife and family is, that's what he talked about," Trump said.

item.title: Warby Parker bets on Google AI glasses for growth, but privacy fears still loom
item.description: Warby Parker is entering the smart glasses market in partnership with Google and Samsung, betting that demand for the artificial intelligence wearables will balloon in the coming years.

item.title: Samsung in talks to buy data center cooling firm Modine
item.description: The companies are discussing a potential deal that could come together as soon as the coming weeks, the report added.

item.title: FBI says US has seized $1.2 billion worth of cryptocurrency stolen from Binance
item.description: Typically in those situations, the U.S. government will file a claim of forfeiture with a judge, who will then determine who has a legitimate claim to the recovered funds.

item.title: ‘I’m a piece of sh--’: Jensen Huang’s last hours as Nvidia CEO
item.description: For the decades he spent building Nvidia into a multitrillion-dollar AI chip behemoth, Huang was famous for his attention to the tiniest of details, from chip architecture to the compensation packages of even the most junior employees at the company. Now, in the eyes of the people in the room, he had given up.

item.title: Widespread outage hits Microsoft email, other apps
item.description: Nearly 1,30,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 pm. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn't send and receive emails or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether.

Alphabet's debut Hong Kong, Singapore bond sales draw about $5 billion in early orders
item.description: The strong order books give Alphabet flexibility to increase its planned financing as it accelerates investment in AI infrastructure, even as recent volatility in technology shares has made investors more selective.

item.title: Taiwan's Foxconn reports 34% rise in Q3 profit, beats forecasts
item.description: Net profit for the July to September period for Nvidia's biggest server maker and Apple's top iPhone assembler was T$77.5 billion ($2.35 billion), versus an LSEG consensus estimate of T$69.6 billion and compared with T$57.7 billion a year earlier.

item.title: AI boom powers Siemens to record annual profit
item.description: German engineering giant Siemens posted record annual profit on Thursday and said it saw growth ahead as the artificial intelligence boom sweeps up European companies in its supply chain. Siemens said it expected further growth in the current business year, guiding for sales growth of between nine and 11 percent across the company as well as broadly stable or higher profit margins at its two biggest divisions.

item.title: Meta India MD on child sexual abuse material, Muse AI and WhatsApp Pay
Chinese woman accused of spying on Nvidia chief entered Taiwan 8 times
item.description: The woman accused of spying for Beijing during an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang visited Taiwan a total of eight times in 2024 and 2025, a Taiwanese government minister said Thursday. Chiu said records show that Alice Huang visited Taiwan three times in 2024 and five times in 2025.

item.title: Nvidia working with outside firm to identify CEO candidates
item.description: The board is weighing the idea of naming a temporary chief while searching for a permanent one, the person said, asking not to be identified because the information isn’t public.

item.title: South Korea's Lee says Samsung chip packaging expansion to spur $30 billion additional investment
item.description: Lee made the comment during a groundbreaking ceremony for part of theinvestment plans that Samsung affiliates announced in July.

item.title: House Republicans push for Nvidia's Jensen Huang to testify, float subpoena over spy allegations
item.description: A trio of House Republicans are unlikely to allow Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to send his company's general counsel to answer questions on his behalf about his alleged relationship with a Chinese spy, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

item.title: Trump's ties to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in the spotlight
item.description: President Donald Trump's close ties with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang ​have come under renewed scrutiny after revelations about the billionaire executive's affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

item.title: Alleged Chinese spy in Nvidia scandal is living in Beijing
item.description: Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese spy in a scandal that has engulfed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, has returned to her home country, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday, citing people

item.title: Could Huang, Nvidia and company's board be held liable over affair scandal?
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is under scrutiny due to rumored connections with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. An independent committee of directors is investigating potential implications for Nvidia and its stakeholders. Various legal actions, including a proposed class action lawsuit, are being explored by investors. Federal securities regulators may also investigate for possible violations of disclosure laws. The outcome of these investigations could impact the company's future and stock value.

item.title: India blocked 129 betting websites on basis of fake high court orders: Report
item.description: India's government ordered internet providers to block 129 betting websites based on fraudulent high court orders. Investigations have been initiated after it was revealed that these court orders were fake. The Rajasthan and Allahabad High Courts confirmed that the supposed orders did not exist in their records. Concerns about the authenticity of legal documents are growing due to technology advancements.

item.title: TSMC to invest up to USD 1 billion in Anthropic, OpenAI
item.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) has approved investments of up to USD 1 billion in two major Artificial Intelligence companies, Anthropic and OpenAI, as the world's largest dedicated semiconductor foundry expands its strategic presence in the technology ecosystem.
